title: Remote sensing atlas

maps.title: The currents that wrap the world
maps.source: NOAA Global Drifter Program; drogue centered at 15 m
maps.caption: Climatological seasonal circulation, not a real-time field. Animated particles are illustrative integrations, not observed drifter tracks.

maps.title: Light through four bands
maps.source: Copernicus Sentinel-2 Level-2A COG via Element 84 Earth Search STAC
maps.caption: Cloud-masked centered-covariance PCA of Sentinel-2 B2/B3/B4/B8 surface reflectance, displayed as PC3/PC2/PC1 RGB.

maps.title: Lighthouse Reef
maps.caption: The reef is visible from orbit; its famous blue circle is a collapse structure, not an ocean current. The hole is about 305 m across and 123 m deep.
maps.source: NASA/METI/AIST/Japan Space Systems & U.S./Japan ASTER Science Team
maps.displayDate: Satellite imagery composite; acquisition dates vary by tile

maps.title: The reef in a heatwave
maps.caption: Satellite-derived Degree Heating Weeks show accumulated thermal stress across the reef on 15 March 2024. DHW summarizes heat stress; it is not a direct observation of coral condition.
maps.source: NOAA Coral Reef Watch v3.1 DHW · 5 km · 15 Mar 2024

maps.title: A coast that keeps moving
maps.caption: Barrier islands, inlets, and shoals form a restless edge. Satellite imagery shows the shoreline; it does not by itself measure a long-term erosion rate.
maps.source: Esri World Imagery; NOAA National Geodetic Survey coastal mapping
maps.displayDate: Satellite imagery composite; acquisition dates vary by tile

maps.title: Amaila Falls, Guyana
maps.caption: China Railway Group was selected for a proposed Amaila Falls project in 2021. This map marks the proposed site; the cited records do not establish an operating dam or substantiate the claim that it is unregulated.
maps.source: Esri World Imagery; Guyana Energy Agency; Guyana DPI (2021)
maps.displayDate: Satellite imagery composite; acquisition dates vary by tile

maps.title: Point Nemo
maps.kicker: SOUTH PACIFIC · OCEANIC POLE OF INACCESSIBILITY
maps.caption: The point farthest from land lies beneath the South Pacific gyre. Here, the surface gives few clues to the abyssal landscape and slow, basin-scale circulation below.
maps.source: Esri World Imagery; NOAA National Ocean Service
maps.displayDate: Satellite imagery composite; acquisition dates vary by tile

maps.title: The Amazon runs out to sea
maps.caption: A daily satellite-informed surface-salinity field across the Amazon plume. Freshwater fans into the tropical Atlantic; the broad grid resolves basin-scale structure, not the narrow plume edge or estuarine channels.
maps.source: NOAA CoastWatch daily SMAP SSS · 0.25° grid · 15 Mar 2024
